text:
Here is a comprehensive, numbers-driven turnaround plan for the school. 

### **Executive Summary**
The school is currently facing a structural deficit driven by two main factors: **poor fee collection (70%)** and an **unsustainable student-to-teacher ratio (18:1)**. Because the Board has ruled out fee increases, the turnaround must focus entirely on aggressive collection enforcement and cost rationalization. 

By implementing this plan, the school will transition from a **GHS 238,000 annual deficit** to a **GHS 371,600 annual surplus** within 12 months.

---

### **The Financial Baseline vs. The Turnaround Target**

| Metric | Current State (As-Is) | Target State (To-Be) | Variance |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Enrollment** | 400 pupils | 400 pupils | 0 |
| **Termly Fee** | GHS 1,800 | GHS 1,800 | GHS 0 |
| **Gross Potential Revenue (3 terms)** | GHS 2,160,000 | GHS 2,160,000 | GHS 0 |
| **Collection Rate** | **70%** | **90%** | **+20%** |
| **Actual Revenue Collected** | **GHS 1,512,000** | **GHS 1,944,000** | **+GHS 432,000** |
| **Number of Teachers** | 22 | 17 | -5 |
| **Teacher Salary Expense (68% of cost)** | GHS 1,190,000 | GHS 919,600 | -GHS 270,400 |
| **Non-Teacher Expense (32% of cost)** | GHS 560,000 | GHS 504,000 (10% cut) | -GHS 56,000 |
| **Total Expenditure** | **GHS 1,750,000** | **GHS 1,423,600** | **-GHS 326,400** |
| **Net Position (Profit/Loss)** | **-GHS 238,000** | **+GHS 520,400** | **+GHS 758,400** |

---

### **The 3-Pillar Turnaround Plan**

#### **Pillar 1: Revenue Assurance (The 90% Collection Drive)**
The school is currently subsidizing 30% of its student body. We must increase collection to 90% in Year 1.
*   **Direct Debit & MoMo Pay:** Partner with a local bank or MTN/Telecel to set up automated direct debits or mandatory Mobile Money (MoMo) payment channels. 
*   **The 50-30-20 Rule:** Parents must pay 50% of fees before Day 1 of the term, 30% by Week 4, and the final 20% by Week 8.
*   **Strict Exclusion Policy:** Students with outstanding balances after Week 8 will not be allowed to attend classes or sit for exams. 

#### **Pillar 2: Staff Rationalization (Reducing the Teacher Count)**
With 400 pupils and 22 teachers, the student-to-teacher ratio is 18:1. While educationally desirable, it is financially unviable. 
*   **Layoffs:** Reduce the teaching staff from 22 to 17. This adjusts the student-to-teacher ratio to a still-reasonable **23.5:1**.
*   **Class Merging:** Combine double-stream classes where enrollment is low (e.g., if there are two streams of JHS 1 with 15 students each, merge them into one class of 30).
*   **Salary Savings:** This action saves **GHS 270,400** annually (assuming an average teacher cost of GHS 54,080/year).

#### **Pillar 3: Operational Cost Cutting**
*   Reduce non-salary operational expenses (utilities, printing, security, maintenance) by 10% through renegotiating supplier contracts and digitizing report cards/newsletters to save on paper and ink.
*   **Savings:** **GHS 56,000** annually.

---

### **Unpopular Recommendations & Why We Must Do Them**

To save the school from bankruptcy, the Board must brace for severe pushback on three specific fronts:

#### **1. Laying off 5 Teachers (Redundancy)**
*   **Why it will be unpopular:** It will damage morale among the remaining staff, anger the affected teachers, and likely cause concern among parents who value small class sizes.
*   **Why we must do it anyway:** Teacher salaries make up 68% of the budget. It is impossible to balance the books without touching payroll. A student-teacher ratio of 23.5:1 is still far superior to the Ghanaian public school average (often 35+:1) and remains highly competitive for a private school. Survival of the institution must take precedence over individual employment.

#### **2. Implementing a Strict "No Pay, No School" Policy**
*   **Why it will be unpopular:** Turning children away at the school gate because their parents haven't paid is emotionally difficult, culturally sensitive, and will lead to accusations of being "heartless" or "money-minded."
*   **Why we must do it anyway:** A 70% collection rate means the paying 70% of parents are carrying the financial burden for the non-paying 30%. This is unsustainable. Compassion without financial viability is suicide; if the school closes down, 100% of the pupils lose their education, and all 22 teachers lose their jobs.

#### **3. Freezing Teacher Salary Increments for 12 Months**
*   **Why it will be unpopular:** In Ghana’s current high-inflation environment, a salary freeze is effectively a real-terms pay cut. Teachers will complain, and some may threaten to leave.
*   **Why we must do it anyway:** The school is in a cash-flow crisis. Any increase in payroll expenses this year will wipe out the gains of the staff rationalization. Once the school achieves the target surplus of GHS 520,400, the Board can introduce a performance-based bonus pool in Year 2 to reward the remaining 17 teachers.
